The root cause of the repeated error is that f-strings are being used with multi-line strings without proper escaping or continuation. This causes a syntax error because Python interprets the newline inside the f-string as the end of the string, leaving the rest unmatched.

To fix this, I will avoid using f-strings for multi-line outputs and instead use regular `print()` statements with string concatenation or separate `print()` calls.

I will now proceed to fix the issue and complete the analysis.

{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float, removing commas
# First, ensure the string is clean: replace commas if present
# Then convert to float
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Remove QA orders (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_mask = df['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99
num_qa = qa_mask.sum()
print('Number of QA orders:', num_qa)

# Remove refunded orders
refunded_mask = df['status'] == 'refunded'
num_refunded = refunded_mask.sum()
print('Number of refunded orders:', num_refunded)

# Filter out QA and refunded orders
valid_orders = df[~qa_mask & ~refunded_mask]

# Group by channel and sum revenue
revenue_by_channel = valid_orders.groupby('channel')['revenue_clean'].sum()

# Print the result
print('Revenue by channel (after filtering):')
print(revenue_by_channel)

# Find the channel with the highest revenue
best_channel = revenue_by_channel.idxmax()
max_revenue = revenue_by_channel.max()

print('Channel with highest revenue:', best_channel)
print('Max revenue:', max_revenue)"}
